description: Assesses the appropriate deployment and release strategy based on deployment preference, team capability, availability requirements, and service type.

recommendation.rationale: High-availability containerised services with experienced teams benefit from GitOps-based deployment with progressive delivery (canary or blue-green). This provides automated, auditable deployments with the ability to detect and roll back problematic releases before they affect all users.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires platform engineering capability; GitOps tooling needs initial setup investment but reduces ongoing deployment risk
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Pipeline maintenance, canary threshold tuning, GitOps repository management, and deployment monitoring

costConsiderations.runningCosts: CI/CD pipeline execution costs; GitOps controller infrastructure; canary infrastructure during deployments
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: GitOps tooling setup; pipeline development; team training on progressive delivery

recommendation.rationale: Serverless deployments benefit from built-in traffic shifting capabilities that allow gradual rollout of new function versions. This provides safe deployments without managing deployment infrastructure, with automatic rollback on error rate increases.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Standard development team can manage; serverless deployment tooling handles most complexity
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Pipeline updates, deployment configuration reviews, and rollback procedure testing

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Minimal; serverless deployment costs are negligible compared to runtime costs
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Deployment framework setup; CI/CD pipeline configuration

recommendation.pattern: Simple CI/CD Pipeline with Rolling Deployment
recommendation.rationale: Small teams with limited cloud experience benefit from simple CI/CD pipelines with rolling deployments. This provides automated, repeatable deployments without the complexity of progressive delivery, while still supporting rollback through version management.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Any developer can trigger and monitor deployments; no specialist DevOps role required
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Pipeline dependency updates, deployment script maintenance, and periodic review of deployment success rates

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Low; most CI/CD platforms offer generous free tiers for small teams
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Pipeline setup; deployment script development; team familiarisation

recommendation.rationale: VM-based deployments benefit from immutable infrastructure patterns where new deployments create new VM images rather than updating existing instances. This provides consistent environments, easy rollback (revert to previous image), and eliminates configuration drift.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires infrastructure-as-code skills; image pipeline needs maintenance
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Base image updates, security patching pipeline, image testing, and deployment orchestration maintenance

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Image storage costs; build pipeline compute; temporary duplicate infrastructure during deployments
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Image pipeline development; IaC migration; team training

recommendation.rationale: Without cloud access, deployment relies on on-premises CI/CD servers and configuration management tools. This requires more infrastructure but provides automated, repeatable deployments within the constraints of on-premises environments.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires CI/CD infrastructure management; Jenkins/GitLab administration is a dedicated responsibility
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: CI/CD server patching, plugin updates, agent management, and pipeline maintenance

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Hardware for CI/CD infrastructure; licensing (if applicable); staffing
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: CI/CD server setup; pipeline development; team training

defaultRecommendation.rationale: When no specific conditions strongly favour an alternative, a managed CI/CD service with blue-green deployment provides safe, automated releases with easy rollback. This balances deployment safety with operational simplicity.

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Low; managed CI/CD pricing based on build minutes

commonQuestions: What is the target deployment frequency?
Is there an existing CI/CD platform?
What is the acceptable deployment downtime?
How quickly must rollbacks be executed?
Are there change management or approval requirements?
What environments are needed (dev, test, staging, production)?
evidenceNeeded: Environment strategy (number and purpose of environments)
